title: Adversarial BERT with Robustness-Aware Decoding for Noise-Resilient Legal Document Classification and Summarization
content: Operational legal pipelines ingest scanned filings, heterogeneous citation conventions, and documents whose boilerplate has been rewritten, yet the encoders behind them are evaluated almost entirely on clean, born-digital benchmarks. We take the position that noise in legal text is structured rather than random, and we build a framework on that premise. LegalStruct-Attack defines a perturbation space over five families of legal-structural operators: citation reformatting and corruption, clause renumbering, defined-term perturbation, boilerplate migration, and OCR-realistic character confusion for Latin and Arabic script. Structure-aware adversarial fine-tuning then trains a dual-head encoder under a min–max objective that couples discrete structural perturbation with embedding-space ascent and a segment-level consistency term. Robustness-Aware Decoding (RAD) carries robustness past the encoder into generation by re-scoring candidate tokens according to the variance of their log-likelihood across N noisy re-observations of the input; at zero stability weight it reduces exactly to beam search. Measuring the operator library shows the five families occupy separable regions of the perturbation space: clause renumbering alters 0.2% of characters and yields no out-of-vocabulary tokens, boilerplate migration alters 22.1% and also yields none, and OCR confusion turns every token it touches into an unseen one, so surface edit distance orders these attacks incorrectly. A hand-labeled reliability check of the structural parser reaches 81.7% accuracy after two segmentation failure modes were found and fixed during the evaluation. Fine-tuning runs for four English classification baselines are measured rather than projected and show FreeLB and SMART not out-robusting plain LEGAL-BERT under the structural attack, consistent with embedding-space adversarial training not covering discrete structural perturbations. Results for the proposed method itself, the Arabic track, and summarization are not yet reliably measured and are reported as projected values or flagged pilot diagnostics pending completed runs.
